brief: A spending tracker where categories are geological layers — deeper is necessity, surface is discretionary

dominant_strengths: Conceptually rich metaphor — strata literally encode necessity depth, turning a budget into an evocative cross-section diagram.
Earth-tone palette (cream → ochre → rust → deep red) is harmonious and reinforces the geological narrative cohesively.
Vocabulary system ('Excavations', 'Geological Record', layer naming) extends the metaphor through copy with disciplined consistency.
dominant_weaknesses: Severe text collision in middle column: dollar amounts overlap depth labels (e.g., '$1,245' clashing with '2000-6000m'), a clear craft failure.
Total Monthly Spending pill awkwardly floats over the Survival Core layer, obscuring the $3,890 figure and breaking the strata illusion.
Layer rows are visually uniform rectangles — no proportional height by spend, wasting the metaphor's biggest behavioral affordance.
fix_priorities: Resolve label/amount overlap: separate depth ranges into a secondary metadata line or right-align a dedicated column.
Make layer heights proportional to spend so the cross-section becomes a chart, not just decoration.
Reposition the Total card outside the strata or as a fixed footer to stop occluding Core values.
Tighten typographic hierarchy — layer titles, amounts, and depth meta currently fight at similar weights.
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral and reflective payoff from the metaphor, but behavioral utility suffers because overlapping numbers and non-proportional bars undermine quick spending comprehension.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — the geological-layer framing for necessity vs discretionary spending is executed thematically end-to-end, though craft bugs blunt its functional clarity.
